web_text_verbatim: Anderson & D'Alonzo Odontoid Classification: Type I (tip avulsion, collar for 8 weeks), Type II (base/waist of dens, halothoracic vest or anterior screw), Type III (body of axis, external orthosis).
focus: Odontoid C2 - Types I, II, III conservative vs operative indications
suggested_fix: None needed. Confirmed in Rockwood 10th ed.
quote: Notwithstanding those cases that represent occult craniocervical dissociation, type I fractures are treated in a hard cervical collar for 8 weeks, after which flexion–extension views are obtained to confirm stability. It is, however, important to realize that isolated type I fractures are exceedingly rare. Most nondisplaced type II fractures in young patients are treated in a halothoracic vest, whereas most nondisplaced type III fractures are treated in an external orthosis.
